description: The math arm for LLMs: compute and check numbers from CSV and Excel tables in Python, every number computed by pandas, SciPy and statsmodels with its calculation and rows, or refused with a reason. Tool definitions for function calling (ada.tools) for Claude, Codex and open-source models run with Ollama, vLLM, llama.cpp or LM Studio; a check of any number stated about a table; a map of a folder of files; cross-validated models that predict a column (ada model, ada auto, --explain); and a paper's tables, figures and methods draft built from a study.yml that ada verify rebuilds.
rules: Give a language model ADA's tools with ada.tools.definitions() (or 'anthropic' style) and run its calls with ada.tools.run(name, arguments, root=folder); send back the JSON it returns.
Let ADA compute the numbers: report what it prints, with the calculation and rows it names, instead of computing or estimating them yourself.
Check every number you state about a data file with ada claim (or ada.check_claim) and report verified or unverified with ADA's reason; never call a whole answer verified because one number was.
When a check comes back missing_context or ambiguous_intent, ask the person ADA's clarification question instead of choosing a reading.
For a folder of files, run ada scan first and confirm the proposed links, row meanings and units with the person before combining files.
Before writing study.yml, ask the researcher what one row is, which column identifies a subject or cluster, the design and which analyses were planned; do not guess them.
Run ada build and then ada verify after any change to study.yml or the data, and never edit the files in paper-assets/ by hand.
